_note: The three synthetic sample organizations shipped with the OCI package (Everytown_OCI_Package/03_Sample_Responses). Names, profile lines and descriptions are copied from the sample reports; answers live in ../benchmark/sample_<id>_answers.json. Not real organizations. 'category' is not stated in the package and is assigned here only so the staff view can show a grantee/non-grantee split. 'website_url' uses the reserved .example domain because the samples have no websites.

organizations.description: A neighborhood-rooted violence interruption and youth mentoring group in its third year. Credibility with young people and families is its greatest asset; nearly all back-office function runs through the founder/executive director. Funding is one city contract plus small individual gifts.

An established CVI provider operating hospital-based intervention and street outreach across two precincts. Core systems exist and are used, but they are uneven: the board is functioning yet thin on finance expertise, and evaluation is still mostly output counting. Roughly 80% of revenue is restricted government funding.

A regional anchor organization running CVI programming, a training institute for peer organizations, and a policy shop. Most domains are mature and integrated. The remaining work is at the top of the ladder: an endowment-grade reserve strategy, independent impact evaluation, and modernizing data infrastructure that has not kept pace with headcount.
